description: A two-year, 48 credit point postgraduate degree in Building Information Modelling and digital construction management, taught on campus at the Bruce campus. The structure runs from an introduction to BIM and BIM technology through procurement, project management and research methods to a 12 credit point professional thesis, with graduate certificate and graduate diploma exit points along the way. Students use the University of Canberra BIM Hub, which has VR and AR facilities, 3D laser scanners and industry modelling software. Entry normally requires an undergraduate qualification in architecture, construction, engineering or a related field, with recognition of prior learning available for applicants with several years of relevant work experience. Graduates work as BIM managers and coordinators, digital engineers, project managers and design managers across architecture, construction and infrastructure. It suits built-environment professionals moving into the coordination and data side of projects.

A two-year, 48 credit point conversion master's that sits across business and information technology, for graduates from any field: no prior IT or business informatics study is assumed. The core covers systems analysis, IT security, aligning technology with business needs and a capstone research project, and students choose one focus from no specialisation, Cybersecurity, Data Science or Project Management. Applicants with relevant work experience can enter through the Professional Pathway. The qualification is recognised by the Australian Computer Society at Professional level, which supports ICT career mobility including overseas. Graduates work as business analysts, IT security analysts, data scientists, systems architects and IT project managers. It suits career changers and recent graduates who want a technology qualification that stays connected to how organisations actually use IT, rather than a pure computer science degree.

A part-time, 36 credit point postgraduate counselling degree delivered mostly online over about two years, with 12 study blocks. It combines counselling theory and skills with supervised practice: 200 hours of placement in an approved agency plus a compulsory five-day in-person intensive. Students should expect to travel for placement, and regional students may need to relocate if they cannot secure one locally. Entry is open to graduates from any discipline. The course is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association, so it supports the pathway toward professional registration and membership as a counsellor. Graduates work in mental health services, community organisations, employee assistance programs, schools and private practice. It suits people moving into counselling from another career who want a recognised qualification with a substantial supervised practice component.

A 24 credit point master's for people who already work in education, completed fully online over about 17 months with intakes every two months and one unit at a time. It is not an initial teaching qualification: entry requires current teacher registration, or a three-year education degree plus three years of professional experience. Students take a generalist path or specialise in STEM Education or Educational Leadership, with graduate certificate exit points in either. The coursework centres on analysing education theory, policy and curriculum and building reflective practice. Graduates move into roles such as curriculum coordinator, head of department, instructional leader, student wellbeing lead and deputy principal. It suits practising teachers and school leaders who want a flexible research-informed qualification to support progression, rather than a route into the classroom.

A two-year, 48 credit point master's in education for people who want to work on policy, curriculum and leadership rather than classroom teaching. One thing to be clear on: it is not externally accredited and is not recognised as a teaching qualification in Australia, so it does not lead to teacher registration. The structure is five core units, 27 credit points of electives and a 6 credit point capstone project, with work integrated learning and authentic assessment built through the degree. Study covers research methods, international policy trends and evidence-based program design. Entry is open to people with a three-year education degree, a bachelor's plus an education diploma, or equivalent professional experience. Graduates work as curriculum developers, policy advisers, educational researchers and senior school and sector leaders. It suits education professionals building toward leadership and policy roles.

A one-year, 24 credit point master's in educational leadership, available on campus or blended, made up of eight units covering leadership and management theory, organisational change, comparative education and educational futures, and ending with a research project. Entry requires a bachelor's degree plus at least three years of relevant experience in education or public administration, and IELTS 6.5 for international applicants. It is aimed squarely at people already working in education who are moving toward formal leadership: aspiring and current principals, deputy principals, education officers and administrators. Graduates work as school and system leaders, district and sector administrators and early childhood directors. It suits mid-career educators who want a focused, one-year leadership qualification rather than a broader two-year master's.

A two-year, 48 credit point master's in teaching English to speakers of other languages and foreign language teaching, delivered in blended mode. The coursework covers second language acquisition, TESOL and language teaching methodology, curriculum and assessment, and includes a work integrated learning component of at least 60 hours with Working with Vulnerable People registration required for the practice unit. No prior teaching qualification or experience is required to enter, only a completed bachelor's degree. Note that registration to teach in Australian schools is a separate process and applicants who want school registration should confirm the current requirements with the ACT Teacher Quality Institute. Graduates work as English language teachers, language teachers, adult and community educators, curriculum advisers and in international education. It suits people moving into language teaching from another background.
